title: [YouPass Collect] - Population Growth, Birth Rate & Life Expectancy: 2002–2004
prompt: The table below gives information related to population growth, average birth per woman, life expectancy at birth in countries with different income levels in 2002 and 2004. Summarise the information making comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table provides data on three demographic indicators, namely population growth, average birth per woman, and life expectancy at birth, in high, middle, and low income countries in 2002 and 2004.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, life expectancy rose in all three income groups over the two-year period, while population growth rates and birth rates either declined marginally or remained unchanged. Additionally, low income nations recorded the highest figures for population growth and fertility but the lowest for life expectancy, in stark contrast to wealthier countries.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding population growth and fertility, in 2002, low income countries experienced the fastest population expansion at 2.0%, more than double the rate of high and middle income nations, at 0.8% and 0.9%, respectively. A similar pattern was observed in birth rates, with women in low income countries having an average of 3.9 children, compared to just 2.2 and 1.7 in middle and high income nations. By 2004, population growth in low income countries had fallen slightly to 1.8%, while it slipped to 0.7 in high income countries and remained at 0.9 in middle income ones. Birth rates also decreased modestly in low and middle income nations, to 3.7 and 2.1 respectively, whereas high income countries saw no change.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for life expectancy, people in high income countries could expect to live the longest, at 78 years in 2002, approximately 9 and 20 years longer than those in middle and low income nations, respectively. By 2004, all three groups witnessed modest increases, rising to 78.7, 70.0, and 58.8 years, in that order.
